title: Site ranking via dual-quantile latency fusion and network-health ledger
creator: Aditi Rao
description: Goal: Implement a site (region/zone) ranking algorithm that blends p50 and p95 latency signals with an independent network-health ledger (packet loss, TCP resets, recent routing flaps) to drive region selection and tiered fallback decisions. This ticket defines design, rollout plan, and the initial implementation for a quantile-fusion scorer that produces a single site_score used by the request router. The scorer must be explainable, resistant to short transients, and support per-customer overrides for sticky affinity and compliance constraints.
background: We currently use separate heuristics for p50/p95 and a few ad-hoc network signals. This leads to oscillation when a site has low median latency but sporadic high tail due to transient network events. We need a unified, auditable score that: (1) mixes short-window quantiles, (2) factors in a persistent network-health ledger that decays over time, and (3) exposes a tunable hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping during noisy periods.
proposal_summary: Introduce a 'quantile-meld' score: score = alpha * p50_norm + beta * p95_norm + gamma * net_health_penalty, where p*_norm are normalized to a per-route baseline. Net-health-penalty is derived from a ledger that accumulates events (packet loss spikes, route flaps, infra alerts) with exponential decay. Add a staging gate that requires sustained improvement for N windows before preferring a lower-scored site. Provide a fast fallback path to pre-approved model variants (smaller quantized variants) when a chosen site crosses a hard threshold.
design_decisions: Normalize p50 and p95 to route-specific baselines to avoid cross-route skew.
Use asymmetric weights (beta > alpha) to prefer lower tails when tail-risk matters for a route.
Ledger entries are weighted by severity (0.1..1.0) and decay with half-life configurable per environment.
Introduce 'salvage policy' that allows rollback to warm variant pool if net-health_penalty exceeds threshold for two consecutive windows.
Expose per-customer policies: sticky affinity TTL, allowed fallback variant families, and geographic restrictions.
implementation_notes: Telemetry: add new binned-quantile metrics (5m window) emitting p50/p95 per route and per-site.
Ledger: store recent events in a time-series store (Prometheus histogram+exemplar or ClickHouse events) and materialize a net_health_penalty every minute.
Router: implement scoring function as a small stateless service (site-scoring) called by the route-decision layer; cache scores for 10s.
Fallbacks: integrate with existing variant-escrow API to pull pre-warmed fallback models and ensure token accounting remains consistent.
Testing: unit tests for normalization, integration tests using synthetic latency and packet-loss feeders, and chaos test injecting flaps.
acceptance_criteria: Router chooses sites whose average p95-based tail latency for production traffic improves by >=7% on at least 10% of routes compared to baseline in A/B.
Flip-rate (site switches per-minute per-route) does not increase by more than 5% compared to current system under normal traffic.
When ledger penalties spike, requests are routed to fallback variants within SLOs (p95) and cost delta is within forecasted bounds.
Score computation is logged and tracable for every decision; we can reconstruct the top-3 factors for any routed request within 30s.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (canary): enable scoring for 2 low-traffic routes in us-west with read-only logging for 48h.
Stage 2 (shadow): compute scores for 20 routes and shadow decisions for 72h, validate metrics and flip-rate.
Stage 3 (gradual): enable routing for 10% of traffic across multi-regions, monitor costs and p95 improvements.
Stage 4 (full): 100% enable with per-customer opt-out and dashboard visibility.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overreacting to short transients -> Mitigation: Hysteresis window + ledger decay.
Risk: Score normalization drift across routes -> Mitigation: periodic baseline recomputation and alerts when normalization factors change >15%.
Risk: Excessive cost from fallback variants -> Mitigation: cost guardrail that disables fallbacks if 7-day cost delta exceeds threshold.
Risk: Observability blind spots -> Mitigation: add per-decision traces and a lightweight score-explain endpoint.
qa_and_metrics: Track p50/p95 per route and per-site before/after rollout (1h, 1d, 7d windows).
Measure flip-rate, route latency regression count, and fallback activation frequency.
Add dashboards: 'site_score distribution', 'ledger event rate', 'fallbacks by route', and 'score explain latency'.
